rag.description: Drag with the left mouse button on a Windows desktop through the UIA driver: from an element or a screen point, to an element, a screen point, or by an offset. The step checks the driver, both ends, and its numbers before anything is pressed, grabs and drops at alignment points of elements, paces the cursor in short steps, and releases the button when the driver refuses the drag.

qa.answer: It drags with the left mouse button in a Windows desktop application through the UIA driver, from an element or a screen point, and drops on a target element, at a screen point, or a pixel offset away.
qa.question: What does the InvokeUser32DragAndDrop plugin do?

qa.answer: OnElement, or X and Y, sets the start; Alignment, OffsetX, and OffsetY select the grab point on an element. Target with TargetAlignment, TargetOffsetX, and TargetOffsetY, or TargetX and TargetY, or DeltaX and DeltaY sets the end. Steps and Duration set the path. It stores no outputs.
qa.question: What are the key parameters and outputs of InvokeUser32DragAndDrop?

qa.answer: It runs as an Action task step with the arrow-pointer icon and the ActionRuleModel, in a flow driven by the UIA driver, after the application shows both elements.
qa.question: How does InvokeUser32DragAndDrop fit into an automation workflow?

qa.answer: Keep the application window visible and unobstructed, drop on element points rather than fixed offsets where possible, and raise Steps for applications that redraw while they follow the cursor.
qa.question: What are best practices for using InvokeUser32DragAndDrop?

qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “InvokeUser32DragAndDrop”, onElement for the dragged element as an XPath, and {{$ --Target://List[@AutomationId='DoneList']}} or {{$ --DeltaX:150 --DeltaY:0}} as the argument; without onElement, use {{$ --X:300 --Y:200 --TargetX:640 --TargetY:420}}.
qa.question: How is an InvokeUser32DragAndDrop rule configured?

qa.answer: Any driver other than the UIA driver, a rule with no start, no end, or two forms of one end, a missing element, or a bad Steps, Duration, coordinate, or offset value fails the step before anything is pressed. When the driver refuses the drag, the left button is released and the step fails with the driver error.

description: ### Purpose

InvokeUser32DragAndDrop drags with the left mouse button in a Windows desktop application. The drag starts on an element or at a screen point, and ends on another element, at a screen point, or a number of pixels away.

It asks the UIA driver for the screen point of the source, and of the target when one is set, presses the left button on the source, moves the cursor in short steps, and releases over the target or at the end of the offset.
Flows use it to move items between lists, to reorder rows, and to move splitters and slider handles.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature | Description |
| Target element | Drops on a point of the element named by the Target XPath. |
| Alignment points | Grabs and drops at the center, an edge, or a corner of each element, shifted by pixel offsets. |
| Drag by offset | Moves the element by DeltaX and DeltaY screen pixels when the rule names no target. |
| Stepped path | Moves the cursor in short steps, 10 by default, so applications that wait for the Windows drag threshold start the drag. |
| Paced moves | Spreads the moves over Duration, 300 milliseconds by default. |
| Release on failure | Releases the left button when the driver refuses the drag, so it does not stay pressed on the desktop. |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case | Description |
| List transfers | Move an item from one list or tree to another in a desktop application. |
| Row order | Reorder rows of a grid that supports dragging. |
| Layout handles | Move a splitter or a slider handle by an exact number of pixels. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case | Description |
| Drop checks | Verify that a dropped item appears in its new list. |
| Order checks | Verify that a grid keeps the order a drag sets. |
| Handle limits | Verify that a splitter or a slider stops at its allowed range. |
### Platform
This plugin works on **Windows** only, with the UIA driver.
It moves the real cursor, so the application window must be visible, and it drags with the left button without modifier keys.

edge_cases: Item or list is not found
annotations.expected_result: Invoice 7 is shown in the done list.
annotations.notes: The application window must be visible, because the drag moves the real Windows cursor. Both elements are found before the button is pressed.

description: ### Move an item to another list
The `onElement` value names the list item, and Target names the list to drop on.
Both points are element centers, and the cursor moves in 10 steps over 300 milliseconds.

annotations.notes: Offsets are measured from the point the alignment selects, in screen pixels. TargetOffsetX shifts the drop point sideways in the same way.

description: ### Drop at the top of a target
TargetAlignment and TargetOffsetY place the drop point 4 pixels below the top center of the target row.
Use it when an application inserts above or below a row depending on where the item is dropped.

annotations.expected_result: The left pane is 150 pixels wider.
annotations.notes: A drag by offset needs no target and ends at the grab point plus the offset. The offset is in screen pixels, so it does not follow display scaling.

description: ### Move a splitter by an offset
DeltaX moves the splitter 150 screen pixels to the right.
Steps and Duration slow the move for an application that redraws while it follows the cursor.

edge_cases: Grab point is not on the title strip
annotations.expected_result: The tools panel is docked on the right side of the window.
annotations.notes: Grab a panel where the application starts a drag, which is often its title strip and not its center. Offsets are in screen pixels from the corner the alignment selects.

description: ### Grab a panel by its title strip
Alignment, OffsetX, and OffsetY grab the panel 20 pixels right of and 8 pixels below its top-left corner, where its title strip is.
The panel is dropped on the center of the right dock area.

edge_cases: The window moved or the screen layout changed since the points were taken, so the drag misses its target
A point is outside every screen, so the cursor stops at the nearest screen edge
OnElement is also set, which names two starts and fails the step
annotations.expected_result: The left button is pressed at (300, 200), the cursor moves in steps to (640, 420), and the button is released there.
annotations.notes: Screen points need no element and no locator. Prefer elements where the application exposes them, because element points follow the window when it moves.

description: ### Drag between two screen points
Presses at the screen point (300, 200), moves to (640, 420), and releases there, without an element.
Use this form for a drag recorded in coordinate mode, or for a canvas that exposes no elements.
Selects the point of the dragged element where the drag starts.
The point is a corner, an edge center, or the center of the element bounding box, shifted by the matching offsets.
Defaults to MiddleCenter; an unknown value makes the UIA driver refuse the request.
parameters.name: Alignment

description: Places the point at the bottom center of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the lower middle edge of the element.
values.name: BottomCenter

description: Places the point at the bottom left corner of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the lower left boundary of the element.
values.name: BottomLeft

description: Places the point at the bottom right corner of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the lower right boundary of the element.
values.name: BottomRight

description: Places the point at the horizontal and vertical center of the element bounding box.
It is the default alignment and suits most drags.
values.name: MiddleCenter

description: Places the point at the left edge and vertical center of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the left side of the element.
values.name: MiddleLeft

description: Places the point at the right edge and vertical center of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the right side of the element.
values.name: MiddleRight

description: Places the point at the top center of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the upper middle edge of the element.
values.name: TopCenter

description: Places the point at the top left corner of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the upper left boundary of the element.
values.name: TopLeft

description: Places the point at the top right corner of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the upper right boundary of the element.
values.name: TopRight

description: Sets the horizontal distance of a drag by offset, in screen pixels, where a positive value points right.
It is measured from the grab point: the point of the OnElement element that Alignment, OffsetX, and OffsetY select, or the X and Y screen point.
Use it instead of Target or TargetX and TargetY; setting more than one end, or text that is not a whole number, fails the step.
parameters.name: DeltaX

description: Sets the vertical distance of a drag by offset, in screen pixels, where a positive value points down.
It is measured from the grab point: the point of the OnElement element that Alignment, OffsetX, and OffsetY select, or the X and Y screen point.
Use it instead of Target or TargetX and TargetY; setting more than one end, or text that is not a whole number, fails the step.
parameters.name: DeltaY

description: Sets the total time of the moves between the press and the release.
Accepts a whole number of milliseconds, such as `600`, or a time span, such as `00:00:01`.
Defaults to 300 milliseconds, and a negative value or text that is not a duration fails the step.
parameters.name: Duration

description: Shifts the grab point by this many pixels on the horizontal axis.
A positive value moves the point right, measured from the point the matching alignment selects.
Defaults to 0, and text that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: OffsetX

description: Shifts the grab point by this many pixels on the vertical axis.
A positive value moves the point down, measured from the point the matching alignment selects.
Defaults to 0, and text that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: OffsetY

description: Sets how many moves carry the element from the source to the end point.
More steps give a smoother path for applications that follow the pointer closely.
Defaults to 10, and a value outside 1 to 100 fails the step.
parameters.name: Steps

description: Names the element to drop on, as an XPath, the locator the User32 elements support.
The search starts from the root of the session and waits for the element like any other element.
Use it instead of TargetX and TargetY or DeltaX and DeltaY; setting more than one end, or none, fails the step.
parameters.name: Target

description: Selects the point of the target element where the drag ends.
The point is a corner, an edge center, or the center of the element bounding box, shifted by the matching offsets.
Defaults to MiddleCenter, and is read only when Target is set.
parameters.name: TargetAlignment

description: Places the point at the bottom center of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the lower middle edge of the element.
values.name: BottomCenter

description: Places the point at the bottom left corner of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the lower left boundary of the element.
values.name: BottomLeft

description: Places the point at the bottom right corner of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the lower right boundary of the element.
values.name: BottomRight

description: Places the point at the horizontal and vertical center of the element bounding box.
It is the default alignment and suits most drags.
values.name: MiddleCenter

description: Places the point at the left edge and vertical center of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the left side of the element.
values.name: MiddleLeft

description: Places the point at the right edge and vertical center of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the right side of the element.
values.name: MiddleRight

description: Places the point at the top center of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the upper middle edge of the element.
values.name: TopCenter

description: Places the point at the top left corner of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the upper left boundary of the element.
values.name: TopLeft

description: Places the point at the top right corner of the element bounding box.
Use this alignment when the grab or drop point is near the upper right boundary of the element.
values.name: TopRight

description: Shifts the drop point by this many pixels on the horizontal axis.
A positive value moves the point right, measured from the point the matching alignment selects.
Defaults to 0, and text that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: TargetOffsetX

description: Shifts the drop point by this many pixels on the vertical axis.
A positive value moves the point down, measured from the point the matching alignment selects.
Defaults to 0, and text that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: TargetOffsetY

description: Sets the horizontal screen coordinate, in pixels, where the drag ends and the button is released.
Use it with TargetY instead of Target or DeltaX and DeltaY; a missing TargetY counts as zero.
Setting more than one end, or text that is not a whole number, fails the step.
parameters.name: TargetX

description: Sets the vertical screen coordinate, in pixels, where the drag ends and the button is released.
Use it with TargetX instead of Target or DeltaX and DeltaY; a missing TargetX counts as zero.
Setting more than one end, or text that is not a whole number, fails the step.
parameters.name: TargetY

description: Sets the horizontal screen coordinate, in pixels, where the drag starts when the rule names no OnElement element.
Use it with Y instead of OnElement, for a drag recorded or written as screen points; a missing Y counts as zero.
Setting it together with OnElement, or text that is not a whole number, fails the step.
parameters.name: X

description: Sets the vertical screen coordinate, in pixels, where the drag starts when the rule names no OnElement element.
Use it with X instead of OnElement, for a drag recorded or written as screen points; a missing X counts as zero.
Setting it together with OnElement, or text that is not a whole number, fails the step.
parameters.name: Y

description: Holds the parameters of the drag, such as `{{$ --Target://ListItem[@Name='Archive']}}`.
A rule sets one start, OnElement or X and Y, and one end, Target, TargetX and TargetY, or DeltaX and DeltaY, and may add alignments, offsets, Steps, and Duration.
properties.name: Argument

description: Selects how the OnElement value finds the element to drag.
Xpath is the locator the User32 elements support, and it is the default.
properties.name: Locator

description: Names the element to drag, as an XPath.
The drag starts on the point of this element that Alignment, OffsetX, and OffsetY select.
Leave it out to start at the X and Y screen point instead; setting both, or neither, fails the step, and an element that is not found fails it before anything is pressed.
properties.name: OnElement

summary: Drags with the left mouse button on a Windows desktop: from an element or a screen point, to an element, a screen point, or by a pixel offset.

Grabs at an alignment point of the element, drops at an alignment point of the target or at the end of the offset, moves the cursor in short steps over a set time, and sends the whole drag in one request to the UIA driver.
Runs only on the UIA driver and fails with a clear message on any other driver.
